newsitem.title: GERMANY: German jobless hits record, no relief seen.
newsitem.headline: German jobless hits record, no relief seen.

text.p: German unemployment climbed to a seven-year high in November as economic recovery failed to boost the labour market, the Federal Labour Office said Thursday, adding that there was no relief in sight.
The number of unemployed rose 50,000 to a seasonally adjusted 4.1 million, and the adjusted unemployment rate jumped to 10.7 percent from 10.6 percent in October.
The rise, while expected at the start of winter, was larger than many economists had forecast.
"It's really quite substantially more than expected," James Stewart of SE Banken said. "It's really unclear in which direction the economy is headed."
Economic growth in the third quarter picked up to 2.4 percent year-on-year, according to official data, but is expected to slow again in the final quarter of the year.

Labour Office President Bernhard Jagoda told a news conference that growth would have to be between 2.5 percent and 3.0 percent to turn around the German labour market, which is dogged by structural problems and high wage costs.
"Recovery and growth still don't have the strength to stop the unfavourable development in the labour market," he said.

On an unadjusted basis, the number of Germans out of work rose to 3.942 million in November from 3.867 million. Referring to the unadjusted data, Jagoda said he expected the total to rise above 4 million for the next few months.
